leads.name: [RESOLVED 2026-08-23, delivered as ber_019] Blutbuche (Copper Beech) at Villa Dr. Fraenkel, Kladow (ND 5-56/B)

location.address: Landhausgarten Dr. Max Fraenkel, Luedickeweg 1, 14089 Berlin-Kladow

leads.reason: CHECKED THIS PASS (2026-08-09), per the brief's instruction to confirm walkability before treating it as part of the Pfaueninsel cluster: it is NOT walkable from Pfaueninsel. Villa Dr. Fraenkel sits in Kladow, on the OPPOSITE bank of the Havel from Wannsee/Pfaueninsel; the only public-transport link between the two banks near here is the BVG ferry F10 (Alt-Kladow to Wannsee), a roughly 4.5km, 20-minute crossing on a completely different ferry route from the short Pfaueninsel chain-ferry, and Kladow is a separate destination roughly 4-5km by road/water from the Pfaueninsel core. Register-designated (ND 5-56/B, 'Schoenheit, landeskundliche Gruende', designated 1993-03-02) and the garden itself is a genuine public destination (Landhausgarten Dr. Max Fraenkel, a reopened public garden with visitor centre and gastronomy per berlin.de and visitspandau.de), so this could be a fine standalone lead for a future Kladow-area cluster, or the seed of a second Berlin walk on the Spandau/Kladow side of the Havel, but it does not belong in the Pfaueninsel walk and should not be forced into one afternoon with it. Still needs a second, tree-specific source (age, girth) beyond the register before it could ship on its own. RESOLVED 2026-08-23, per Hidde's 2026-08-13 ruling that a missing age or girth never blocks publication: shipped as ber_019, flagged, using the register for the tree's own designation and berlin.de/berlingarten.de for the garden's public status and history. Note for whoever touches this next: the register's own coordinate (52.442538,13.128787) sits about 270m from the garden's actual mapped grounds, so the published pin uses the garden's own centroid instead and is marked approximate. Do not confuse this tree with the separate, already-documented 120-year-old Blutbuche Naturdenkmal at the Kladow-Center (2019 berliner-woche.de coverage of a crown pruning); that is a different tree at a different address.

C. Vicioso', German name 'Geschlitzblättrige' Trauben-Eiche (a rare cut-leaf variety), location 150m northeast of the Schloss, designation criterion 2a (Seltenheit/rarity). This CONFIRMS the cut-leaf detail a previous pass could only get as an unverifiable WebSearch snippet. (2) BUT: this ordinance PDF and the imported register JSON are the same underlying government designation (both trace to the Bezirksamt Steglitz-Zehlendorf Naturdenkmalverordnung, digitised into the Land Berlin GIS/WFS layer that the JSON was pulled from), so treating them as two INDEPENDENT sources is not honest, they are one official source read twice. (3) Went looking for a real independent tree-specific source: baumkunde.de register entries 2135 ('Eiche auf der Pfaueninsel', GPS E13°7.2423'/N52°25.889' = 52.43148/13.12074, 'ostrich-shaped twisted crown', 5.67m girth, vital Sep 2015, explicitly states NO cut-leaf/Geschlitzblättrige note) and 6402 ('Tuereiche auf der Pfaueninsel', ~250yr, 5.58m girth, 8.5m height) were fetched directly and both match the coordinates of the ALREADY-PUBLISHED ber_011 (2135, ~2m away) and ber_012 (6402, matches Tuereiche by name) respectively, not 6-108/B (24m+ from 2135's coords). ostdeutsches-baumarchiv.de's 'Traubeneiche 1 auf der Pfaueninsel' (Umfang 565cm, 'Schlosswiese, am Weg zwischen den beiden Wiesenteilen, noerdlicher Bereich', species given inconsistently as both Quercus robur on one page and generic Traubeneiche on its own index page) does not match 6-108/B's 'ca. 150m nordoestlich vom Schloss' location either and is likely yet another tree or a mislabelled duplicate of one of the other three. monumentaltrees.com pages (14327, 28796) are blocked (403) to both direct WebFetch and the r.jina.ai proxy (bot-detection page, not the article). Heinrich-von-Kleist-Park is public (de.wikipedia: closed for decades, 'in den fruehen 1980er Jahren war er fuer jedermann betretbar', open to everyone since the early 1980s) and historically rich: it was Berlin's OLD Botanical Garden from 1801 (7.5 hectares) before the garden moved to Dahlem around 1900, and 'ein Teil des vorhandenen Baumbestandes stammt aus dem Botanischen Garten' per both de.wikipedia and the Tempelhof-Schoeneberg district's own Denkmal page (berlin.de). Neither source names which specific surviving trees date from the old Botanical Garden, so tying any of these three named specimens to 1801 planting would be exactly the bridge-claim trap this project has already been burned by once (Baarn); not done. No per-tree second source (age, girth, planting date) found for the catalpa, mulberry or oak individually. Register is the only source. Worth a future pass checking the Kammergericht/Verfassungsgerichtshof's own site (the court occupies the former palace) or a Schoeneberg local-history society for a per-tree account tied to the old Botanical Garden.
